experiments.name: Transactions, filters, persistence, and forced termination
experiments.output: PASS extended transaction, vector, persistence, and recovery tests
experiments.conclusion: The extended test covers rollback, read-own-writes, statement atomicity, clean restart, forced termination, committed deletes, and mid-COMMIT all-or-none recovery.

experiments.name: SQL boundary and error semantics
experiments.output: PASS SQL boundary, atomicity, and error semantics
experiments.conclusion: The test covers BIGINT minimum, Unicode length, invalid vectors, unknown columns, unsupported OR, failed statement atomicity, and restart persistence.

experiments.name: Out-of-cache disk scan
experiments.output: PASS out-of-cache disk scan and filtered TopK
experiments.conclusion: With a 1 MiB cache, a 3000-row vector table is read back from disk and filtered TopK remains correct.

experiments.name: Local contest-shaped benchmark
experiments.output: 10000 rows, 128 dimensions, 1000 queries, K=10; write 2.069445 s, query 0.387468 s; sampled Recall@10 1.0 for filtered and unfiltered groups
experiments.conclusion: This is a local Windows development measurement, not the official Linux cgroup result.

retrospective.summary: The implementation prioritizes the functional admission gate. Commit records are durable before success is returned, incomplete tails are truncated, and visible state is reconstructed only from committed transactions. Exact vector search avoids ANN recall risk.

limitations: The official hidden MySQL cases and complete test driver were not public at the time of this record.
A local Docker daemon was unavailable, so the Dockerfile was build-step reviewed and the same source was built with CMake, but docker build itself was not executed.
The benchmark values come from a Windows development host rather than the official Linux cgroup v2 evaluator.
The student author should add further original explanations, counterexamples, and experimental decisions as the work continues; this file does not invent such evidence.
